description: §19.16.6 (S430 round 4, N1) — a nested helper whose body holds a block-bodied arrow is CALLED BEFORE the defer and DECLARED after it. The per-block defer stack keeps the whole block in place, so the helper is hoisted within its own block exactly as without the defer: n1() = 4 and the deferred D runs at exit (trace "d;"). Identical to the no-defer twin. (The round-3 lowering moved code across the try boundary and threw `count is not a function`.)
rationale: §19.16.6: the lowering wraps the whole block in place; every declaration stays in its original block, so function hoisting is exactly what it is without the defer.
